title: A Multi-robot System for Semi-automated Image-guided Vertebral Augmentation
text:
Vertebral compression fractures, the most common fragility fractures secondary to osteoporosis, are effectively
treated with vertebral augmentation, which rapidly reduces pain and restores function. The goal of this project
is to advance surgical robotics technology for vertebral augmentation to reduce radiation dose, increase safety,
and improve efficacy. This will be accomplished by developing a novel class of tool-mounted robots and a
suite of powerful image-based algorithms for automated intra-operative planning, verification, and control,
integrated in mixed reality for remote actuation and assurance.

title: Genomics Core
text:
GENOMICS CORE: NARRATIVE
The Genomics Core will support the research of the three projects in this P01 by processing all samples to
generate genomic data. Genomic data in this application means information about the genes expressed in each
sample, as well as the chromatin state of the cells, which regulates how genes are expressed. Genomic data
generated by this Core will be used to further advance our understanding of genomic and chromatin
dysregulation in cancer, with the ultimate goal of development of novel therapies to treat hematological cancers.

title: EBV Modulation of Genome Stability in B-cell Lymphoma
text:
Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) is associated with several aggressive B cell cancers, including Burkitt lymphoma and
diffuse large B cell lymphoma. This project will define how EBV alters DNA repair processes in infected B cells,
promoting genome instability and malignant transformation. The findings may help identify new therapeutic
targets for virus-associated cancers.

title: Animal Shared Resource
text: ANIMAL SHARED RESOURCE – PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT The Animal Shared Resource (A-SR) offers integral support to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Cancer Center (CSHL-CC) members by providing high quality animal housing and husbandry services. In addition, highly trained technicians offer advanced services and provide training on a variety of methods, including surgical manipulations, post-surgery monitoring, blood and tissue collection, tissue perfusion, as well as administration of therapeutic agents and viruses. In response to member requests, during the current funding cycle, the A-SR re-established engineered mouse model services, and the A-SR now provides cryopreservation, rederivation, mouse embryonic stem cell targeting, and CRISPR gene editing capabilities, allowing members to generate and preserve novel cancer models. The A-SR is led by Faculty Head Alea Mills, Ph.D., and Director Rachel Rubino, D.V.M. The support provided by the A-SR is critical for allowing the CSHL-CC to realize its mission to unravel the fundamental mechanisms that govern the biology of cancer through collaborative research and technology development while training exceptional cancer scientists to become future leaders in the field. The facility enables key discoveries relevant to the CSHL-CC strategic plan cross-programmatic themes of cancer physiology, molecular drivers of cancer, cancer heterogeneity, and preclinical therapeutics and diagnostics. It has enabled researchers to develop innovative animal models for cancer, which continue to be instrumental in uncovering the genetic and molecular basis of the disease. These include viral transduction models, multi-allele reversible cancer models, and organoid orthotopic engraftment models of human and mouse cancer. In addition, the A-SR is integral to the preclinical testing of cancer therapeutic strategies, thus helping the CSHL-CC achieve the strategic goal of promoting translation of CSHL-CC research. During the current period, 28 CSHL-CC member labs used the A-SR (49% of members), and members accounted for 77% of total usage. The A-SR contributed to 77 member publications. Among them, 45 were in journals with impact factors greater than 10, and 3 feature A-SR staff as co-authors, demonstrating the value the A-SR adds to CSHL-CC member research. In summary, the A-SR provides researchers with the ability to move beyond cell culture and to explore cancer biology, cancer physiology, and cancer medicine in an in vivo context.

title: Modeling ALS Pathogenesis Using Human iPSC-Derived Neuromuscular Organoids
text:
Self-organizing 3D organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells are powerful platforms for modeling
development, physiology, and disease in a human-specific context. This project will establish and validate
iPSC-derived neuromuscular organoids (NMOs) to model amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). By comparing
ALS and isogenic control NMOs, we will identify structural, synaptic, and functional alterations underlying
disease pathology

title: Role of hexokinase 3 in macrophage polarization and cardiac remodeling after myocardial infraction.
text:
Myocardial infarction (MI) is a leading causes of death in the world, and macrophages play a
critical role in the remodeling of the heart after MI. Hexokinases (HK) catalyze the first step in glucose
metabolism by phosphorylating glucose, and one HK isoform (HK3) is predominantly expressed in
macrophages. In this proposal, we will assess whether HK3 plays a role in macrophage polarization
and the mechanism for this process, and will determine whether deletion of HK3 is protective against
cardiac damage after MI.

title: Toward a quantitative understanding of metabolic homeostasis
text:
Metabolic syndrome caused by dysregulation of metabolic pathways is implicated in the pathophysiology of many
common diseases including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, and infectious diseases. The goal of this
project is to better understand the regulation of metabolic homeostasis using a combination of mathematical
modeling and experimental approaches in live cells. A better understanding of metabolic homeostasis has the
potential to lead to novel therapies for common diseases associated with metabolic syndrome.

title: MSK Computational Biology Summer Program
text:
R25 MSK Computational Biology Summer Program: Project Narrative
The MSK Computational Biology Summer Program (CBSP) aims to train the next generation of computer
science savvy students in cancer biology. Biologists are trained to form a hypothesis and provide data to
support it, but in the current big data era, many can’t find the insights they seek in the vast troves of data
they’ve collected. CBSP participants, through exposure to cancer biology topics, can use their skills to develop
new tools and mine big data towards finding the next generation of cancer therapeutics, patient diagnostics,
and furthermore, can uncover novel biological and mechanistic insights into cancer.

title: Hybridization Chain Reaction: Automated Ultrasensitive Multiplex RNA and Protein Imaging
text:
Hybridization Chain Reaction:
Automated Ultrasensitive Multiplex RNA and Protein Imaging
We propose to engineer and commercialize molecular technologies that will enable automated, ultrasensitive,
simultaneous imaging of multiple RNA and protein molecules within sample types critical to drug development,
clinical pathology, and biological research. The resulting products will enable the development of new therapies,
the clinical diagnosis of disease, and the study of human biology and disease.

title: MAGNET: MAKING GENOMICS ACCESSIBLE FOR NEWBORNS IN TEXAS
text:
There is significant health care disparity in access to genomic medicine among sick newborns in broad
areas of Texas. Our proposed work will provide evidence of the impact of a virtual platform for
telegenetic consultation service with low-cost genomic sequencing to reduce this disparity, as well as
determine best practices for implementation.

title: Novel Therapeutic Strategies to Co-Target Undifferentiated Prostate Cancer (PCa) Stem Cells and Bulk PCa Cells
text:
The current R01 project aims to test the validity and efficacy of novel therapeutic strategies targeting AR-/lo prostate
cancer (stem) cells with novel therapeutics such as the ATRi (AZD), which, when used in combination with the
current standard-of-care anti-PCa therapies like ADT/Enza (which target the bulk differentiated AR+ PCa cells),
should help prevent or delay the recurrence of advanced disease and greatly IMPACT mCRPC patient survival.

title: Predicting ARDS trajectory with deep generative models of CT images
text:
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), a clinically defined hypoxemic syndrome, requires mechanical
ventilation to prevent immediate death. Lung protective ventilation and prone positioning decrease mortality, but
individual responses to these interventions, and clinical outcomes, are often unpredictable. Leveraging the latest
developments in artificial intelligence on image synthesis, the goal of this project is to develop, train, and test
deep generative models to predict ARDS progression and treatment responses from early computed tomography
images.

title: Formation, metabolism and cell signaling actions of tryptophan catabolism-derived electrophiles
text:
The research plan is relevant to public health because it explores a novel series of endogenous
products derived from normal tryptophan metabolism that have the potential to modulate cellular
and systemic responses. Understanding the formation and regulation of these products will not
only provide new insights into the biological actions of an essential nutrient, but also has the
potential to open new avenues for the development of therapies aimed at improving conditions in
which tryptophan metabolism is dysregulated. Thus, this proposal is significant to the NIH mission
in that it seeks to apply fundamental knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce
illness and disability.

title: Uncovering the role of thyroid hormone-mediated chromatin remodeling in murine ethanol consumption
text:
Alcohol Use Disorder and thyroid hormone axis dysfunction have long been clinically linked but challenging to
target therapeutically due to off target metabolic effects of peripheral thyroid hormone disruption. To circumvent
these side effects, we have selectively activated thyroid hormone receptors in the brain, which are known
transcription factors and epigenetic modifiers, and shown this treatment is effective to decrease alcohol intake
in mice, though the molecular and epigenetic underpinnings of this relationship are still unknown. This proposal
aims to elucidate the regional and epigenetic mechanisms by which central thyroid hormone receptor activation
suppresses alcohol drinking to identify novel targets for alcohol use disorder.

title: The Nathan Schnaper Intern Program in Translational Cancer Research
text:
Project Narrative.
Advances in cancer research and care have reduced deaths from all cancers by 31% in the past three decades;
however, cancer remains a major public health concern with 2 million new cases projected for the US in 2024.
Reducing the cancer burden requires input at all levels, from basic research and clinical trials to screening,
community outreach and survivorship. The Nathan Schnaper Intern Program in Translational Cancer Research
at the University of Maryland Greenebaum Comprehensive Cancer Center is an immersive 10-week
undergraduate internship that provides future cancer researchers and caregivers with experience across the
cancer continuum that will equip them to address the most pressing areas in the field.

title: Determining the role for lncRNAs in TB infection in macrophages
text:
There is a critical need to identify and understand mechanisms of cellular immunity that regulate inflammation
and control bacterial replication during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. With known roles in
immunity, lncRNAs represent a massive family of RNAs with potential to impact Mtb pathogenesis. By
employing innovative high-throughput screening approaches, this proposal aims to implicate novel lncRNAs in
the macrophage response to Mtb, with the goal of identifying new targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: Oral THC consumption during adolescence and its impact on adult mouse brain
text:
Cannabis use by adolescents is rising rapidly and yet little is known about its effect on the developing brain and
ensuing consequences on adulthood behavior. This R01 grant proposal will determine the impact of voluntary
oral use of the phytocannabinoid, 9-tetrahydrocannabinoid (THC, formulated in gelatin) by adolescent mice on
adulthood aversive and motivated behaviors, and whether this impact is dampened by cannabidiol (CBD) co-
administration. Our work will increase the mechanistic understanding of the specific dysregulation of brain
function that is responsible for persistent behavioral deficits associated with THC use during adolescence.

title: Mechanisms of antibiotic failure during osteomyelitis
text:
A key step in the treatment of invasive bacterial infection is the selection of antibiotics that are capable of killing
the causative pathogen. Yet, many patients fail to improve despite treatment with antibiotics that have proven in
vitro activity against the invading bacteria. The objective of this proposal is to understand the bacterial and host
factors underlying antibiotic failure during invasive Staphylococcus aureus infection of bone.

title: Integrating histology and translational imaging of the human cochlea
text:
The ability to non-invasively image and interpret details of cochlear anatomy would be extremely valuable for
helping patients with ear disease and of great scientific use. To develop this capability, we will use optical
coherence tomography (OCT) with low-risk techniques to image into the intact cochlea of very fresh human
specimens, then process histology to learn how to accurately interpret microstructural anatomy in OCT images.
We will also advance, build, and carefully test an OCT endoscope in cadaveric specimens, then trial our new
OCT endoscope to image the cochlea in patients.

title: Modeling the Emergence Cascade: From Wildlife Pathogen Circulation to Human Outbreak Amplification
text:
Pandemics arise when animal viruses spillover into humans and amplify into large outbreaks,
yet current preparedness strategies remain largely reactive. This program will deliver a
comprehensive predictive framework that unites wildlife health, viral burden, and human
transmission dynamics to forecast epidemic potential spatially and across pathogens. By
revealing early warning signals and providing actionable risk maps, this work will transform One
Health surveillance and strengthen our ability to prevent future pandemics.
